hints: The cell has negligible internal resistance, so its 1.3 V e.m.f. is the potential difference across X.
Use V = IR and rearrange to I = V / R.
walkthrough: With negligible internal resistance, the potential difference across X is 1.3 V.
The current in X is 1.2 A.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses I = 1.3 / 1.1 and obtains 1.2 A, allowing a correctly rounded equivalent.

hints: Use I = Anvq and rearrange it for the drift speed v.
Use the current from part (a)(i), n = 8.5 × 10²⁸ m⁻³, q = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and A = 4.7 × 10⁻⁷ m².
walkthrough: The drift-current relationship is I = Anvq.
Rearrange to v = I / (Anq).
This gives v = 1.88 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹.
The average drift speed is 1.9 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Rearranges I = Anvq and substitutes the current, number density, electron charge and wire area correctly.
Obtains a drift speed of 1.9 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹, allowing a correctly rounded equivalent.

hints: Start with R = ρL / A and rearrange for ρ.
Convert the 45 cm wire length to 0.45 m before substituting the resistance and cross-sectional area.
walkthrough: Use R = ρL / A, so ρ = RA / L.
The wire length is 45 cm = 0.45 m.
Therefore the resistivity is 1.1 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m.

ai_rubric.observable: Rearranges the resistivity relationship to ρ = RA / L.
Substitutes R = 1.1 Ω, A = 4.7 × 10⁻⁷ m² and L = 0.45 m.
Obtains 1.1 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m, allowing a correctly rounded equivalent.

hints: Adding an identical resistor in parallel provides another path for charge, so compare the combined resistance with the original 1.1 Ω.
The cell p.d. is unchanged; use V = IR to link the smaller total resistance to the ammeter reading.
walkthrough: Two identical wires in parallel have a combined resistance smaller than the resistance of either wire alone.
The ideal cell keeps the potential difference across the parallel combination unchanged.
From I = V / R, a smaller total resistance at the same potential difference gives a larger total current.
Therefore the ammeter reading increases.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the total resistance decreases while the potential difference remains the same.
Concludes that the ammeter reading increases.

hints: Although the total current changes, consider the p.d. and resistance of the unchanged branch X itself.
Use I = Anvq for X after deciding whether its branch current changes.
walkthrough: Wire X remains directly across the same ideal 1.3 V cell, and its resistance is unchanged.
Its branch current is therefore unchanged by I = V / R, even though the total current from the cell increases.
For the same wire, n, A and q are unchanged; I = Anvq then gives the same drift speed.
Therefore the average drift speed in X stays the same.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the drift speed in X is unchanged because the current in the unchanged branch X remains the same.
